programming-os.name: Computer Programming and Operating System Lab
programming-os.description: This laboratory is designed for the students to perform programming and system-level tasks. It provides a robust environment for learning C/C++, Java, Python, and Operating System concepts such as shell scripting and kernel management.
objectives: Mastering core programming languages
Learning OS kernels and shell scripting
Developing complex algorithms
Collaborative coding practices

database.name: Database and Data Warehouse Lab
database.description: Equipped with industry-standard database management systems, this lab allows students to design, implement, and manage complex databases. It also focuses on data warehousing and big data analytics.
equipment: Large Display Monitors for Query Analysis
objectives: Designing Relational Databases
Executing advanced SQL queries
Implementing Data Warehousing solutions
Understanding NoSQL and Big Data

digital-embedded.name: Digital and Embedded System Lab
digital-embedded.description: Focuses on the intersection of hardware and software. Students work with digital logic kits, FPGA boards, and various embedded systems to build real-world applications.
objectives: Designing Digital Logic Circuits
Programming Embedded Controllers
FPGA Prototyping
Hardware-Software Integration

network-hardware.name: Network and Hardware Lab
network-hardware.description: A specialized lab for computer networking and hardware maintenance. Students learn to configure routers, switches, and understand the physical architecture of computer systems.
objectives: Configuring LAN/WAN networks
Network Security Implementation
PC Hardware troubleshooting
Learning OSI and TCP/IP protocols

microprocessor.name: Microprocessor and Interfacing Lab
microprocessor.description: Provides hands-on experience with microprocessor kits (8086/8088) and microcontroller interfacing. Students learn assembly language programming and how to interface sensors and motors.
objectives: Writing Assembly Language Programs
Interfacing hardware with microprocessors
Building robotic prototypes
Understanding Computer Architecture

ict.name: Computer Programming & Software Engineering Lab
ict.description: This laboratory is designed for students to master fundamental coding, programming methodologies, software design architectures, and database configurations. It hosts powerful workstations running Linux and Windows, equipped with top-tier development suites.
objectives: Develop strong problem-solving and algorithmic logic
Master C/C++, Java, and Python frameworks
Implement software design patterns and SDLC methodologies

ict.name: Signal Processing & Telecommunication Lab
ict.description: A highly specialized laboratory focusing on digital signal processing, signal modulations, antenna systems, and telecommunication hardware interfacing. Students gain practical insights into the physical transmission layer of ICT systems.
objectives: Analyze signal behavior in time and frequency domains
Perform analog and digital modulation experiments
Understand optical fiber communications and signal propagation

ict.name: Cybersecurity & Computer Networks Lab
ict.description: Focuses on network administration, security enforcement, and threat detection. Students work on configuring physical routing systems, analyzing packets, and testing penetration methods in secure sandbox environments.
objectives: Configure complex local and wide-area networks
Design secure firewalls and access control lists
Understand vulnerability assessment and cryptographic principles

ict.name: VLSI & Embedded System Lab
ict.description: Provides hands-on experience in VLSI chip design, digital logic verification, and embedded computing systems. Students interface microcontrollers with physical systems to build automated automation solutions.
objectives: Write Hardware Description Languages (VHDL/Verilog)
Program microcontrollers for sensor interfacing and motor control
Design and test integrated circuit blocks

strength-of-materials-lab.name: Strength of Materials Lab
strength-of-materials-lab.description: Focuses on studying the behavior of solid materials under various forms of stress and strain. Students conduct tensile, compressive, shear, and torsion tests on metals, alloys, and composites to understand material failure limits and elasticity.
objectives: Determining tensile and compressive strength of materials
Analyzing stress-strain curves and Poisson's ratio
Investigating impact resistance and fracture toughness
Experimental validation of beam deflection theories

mechanics-of-machinery-lab.name: Mechanics of Machinery Lab
mechanics-of-machinery-lab.description: Dedicated to the kinematic and dynamic study of mechanical linkages, cams, gear trains, and gyroscopes. Students verify mechanical advantage, balancing of rotating masses, and vibration behaviors in mechanical systems.
equipment: Gear Train and Epicyclic Gear Sets
objectives: Analyzing kinematics of planar mechanisms and linkages
Studying static and dynamic balancing in rotating machinery
Understanding governor performance and speed control
Investigating gyroscopic couples and stabilization

thermodynamics-lab.name: Thermodynamics Lab
thermodynamics-lab.description: Equipped with state-of-the-art apparatus for investigating thermodynamic laws, gas behavior, vapor compression cycles, and thermal conductivity. Hands-on testing helps students bridge theoretical thermal physics with practical systems.
objectives: Measuring calorific values of fuels
Verifying First and Second Laws of Thermodynamics
Determining saturation temperature and pressure relations
Evaluating performance of compressors and heat engines

heat-engine-lab.name: Heat Engine Lab
heat-engine-lab.description: Focuses on internal and external combustion engines. Students analyze four-stroke and two-stroke petrol and diesel engines, dynamometer loading, fuel consumption rates, indicated horsepower, and exhaust gas emissions.
equipment: Four-Stroke Multi-Cylinder Petrol Engine Test Rig
Single-Cylinder Diesel Engine with Hydraulic Dynamometer
Fuel Flow Rate and Air Intake Sensors
objectives: Conducting brake thermal efficiency and volumetric efficiency tests
Constructing indicator diagrams and heat balance sheets
Analyzing engine emissions and fuel consumption characteristics
Studying fuel injection and ignition mechanisms

heat-transfer-lab.name: Heat Transfer Lab
heat-transfer-lab.description: Provides practical experimentation in conduction, convection (natural and forced), and thermal radiation. Students experiment with heat exchangers, pin fins, and lagged pipe setups to compute heat transfer coefficients.
equipment: Shell and Tube Heat Exchanger Apparatus
Thermal Conductivity of Liquids and Solids Bench
Critical Heat Flux & Boiling Demonstration Unit
objectives: Measuring thermal conductivity of diverse materials
Calculating overall heat transfer coefficients in heat exchangers
Demonstrating natural vs forced convection dynamics
Validating Stefan-Boltzmann Law for blackbody radiation

refrigeration-and-air-conditioning-lab-2.name: Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Lab
refrigeration-and-air-conditioning-lab-2.description: Specializes in modern HVAC systems, cooling cycle efficiency, psychrometric properties of moist air, duct layout design, and eco-friendly refrigerant performance under varying load conditions.
objectives: Determining Coefficient of Performance (COP) of cooling units
Executing psychrometric chart analysis for HVAC design
Analyzing refrigerant phase transitions on pressure-enthalpy (P-h) diagrams
Troubleshooting commercial refrigeration circuits

fluid-mechanics-and-machinery-lab.name: Fluid Mechanics and Machinery Lab
fluid-mechanics-and-machinery-lab.description: Dedicated to the study of fluids at rest and in motion. Facilities include open channel flow flumes, pipe friction setups, Pelton wheels, Francis turbines, and centrifugal pump test benches for hydraulic performance analysis.
equipment: Pelton Wheel and Francis Turbine Test Rigs
Venturimeter and Orifice Meter Calibration Setup
Flow Over Notches and Weirs Flume
objectives: Verifying Bernoulli's equation and continuity principles
Calibrating flow measurement devices in closed conduits
Evaluating operating characteristics of impulse and reaction turbines
Calculating friction factors and head losses in pipes and fittings

cad-and-simulation-lab.name: CAD & Simulation Lab
cad-and-simulation-lab.description: High-end computational center equipped with parametric CAD, CAM, and FEA/CFD simulation suites. Students learn 3D mechanical drafting, structural stress analysis, thermal simulations, and aerodynamic flow modeling.
objectives: Creating precision 3D mechanical part and assembly models
Conducting finite element analysis (FEA) for stress distribution
Simulating fluid dynamics and thermal dissipation using CFD
Generating manufacturing production drawings with GD&T

machine-shop-and-production-process-lab-.name: Machine Shop and Production Process Lab
machine-shop-and-production-process-lab-.description: A comprehensive industrial manufacturing facility where students learn turning, milling, shaping, drilling, and grinding. Practical machining experience instills engineering tolerances, tool geometry, and production planning.
objectives: Operating conventional machine tools safely and accurately
Performing precision turning, taper turning, and threading
Executing gear cutting and keyway milling operations
Understanding chip formation, cutting speeds, and tool wear

welding-shop-2.name: Welding Shop
welding-shop-2.description: Specialized training area for metal joining processes. Students practice Shielded Metal Arc Welding (SMAW), Gas Metal Arc Welding (MIG/MAG), Gas Tungsten Arc Welding (TIG), and oxy-acetylene gas welding and cutting.
equipment: Protective Welding Helmets and Fume Extractors
objectives: Mastering manual metal arc and gas welding techniques
Learning weld joint preparation and edge alignment
Preventing weld defects like porosity and undercut
Practicing industrial safety protocols in thermal joining

foundry-shop.name: Foundry Shop
foundry-shop.description: Hands-on facility for sand casting, pattern making, mould cavity preparation, core boxes, metal melting, and pouring. Students witness molten metal solidification and learn casting defect prevention.
equipment: Foundry Sand Mullers and Sieve Analyzers
objectives: Fabricating wooden patterns with shrinkage allowances
Preparing green sand moulds with gating and riser systems
Melting and casting non-ferrous metals safely
Inspecting cast products for shrinkage and blowholes

measurement-and-instrumentation-lab-2.name: Measurement and Instrumentation Lab
measurement-and-instrumentation-lab-2.description: Focuses on engineering metrology and sensor systems. Students calibrate micrometers, verniers, dial indicators, coordinate measurements, surface roughness testers, and electronic sensors for pressure and temperature.
equipment: Dial Gauges, Bore Gauges, and Slip Gauges
LVDT and Load Cell Transducer Kits
objectives: Mastering precision dimensional and angular measurement
Calibrating mechanical and digital measuring instruments
Assessing surface roughness profiles and roundness
Understanding sensor response, hysteresis, and error analysis

materials-and-metallurgy-lab.name: Materials and Metallurgy Lab
materials-and-metallurgy-lab.description: Covers microstructure examination, specimen polishing, chemical etching, and heat treatment. Students study phase diagrams, grain boundaries, and the effects of annealing, quenching, and tempering on steel.
equipment: Inverted Metallurgical Microscopes with Digital Cameras
Chemical Etching and Fume Hood Station
objectives: Preparing metallographic specimens from cutting to mirror polishing
Observing microstructure of ferrous and non-ferrous alloys
Applying heat treatment cycles (hardening, tempering, annealing)
Correlating microstructural phases with mechanical hardness

drawing-lab-2.name: Drawing Lab
drawing-lab-2.description: Dedicated drafting studio with large drafting tables, drafting machines, and projection systems where undergraduate students master orthographic projection, isometric views, sectioning, and engineering drawings.
equipment: Mini Drafters and Precision Rule Sets
Geometric Solid and Mechanical Part Models
objectives: Mastering first and third angle orthographic projection
Drafting sectional, isometric, and assembly drawings
Applying standard dimensioning, tolerancing, and surface symbols
Developing spatial visualization skills essential for mechanical design

production-process-lab.name: Machine Shop and Production Process Lab
production-process-lab.description: The Machine Shop and Production Process Lab provides comprehensive hands-on training in conventional machining and modern manufacturing operations. Students gain practical experience on engine lathes, shaper machines, milling machines, drill presses, and grinding apparatus, learning metal removal principles, chip formation, tool geometry, surface roughness measurement, and precision manufacturing tolerances.
equipment: Universal Milling Machine with Indexing Head
Cutting Force Dynamometers & Precision Vernier Height Gauges
objectives: Mastering fundamental metal cutting mechanisms and chip morphology
Operating manual and semi-automatic machine tools under industrial tolerances
Evaluating machining parameters (speed, feed, depth of cut) on tool wear and surface finish
Understanding industrial machining safety and workpiece clamping techniques

simulation-lab.name: Foundry and Welding Shop
simulation-lab.description: The Foundry and Welding Shop is designed to impart fundamental and practical knowledge of metal joining processes and molten metal casting technology. The facility houses modern shielded metal arc welding (SMAW), gas metal arc welding (GMAW), tungsten inert gas (TIG) welding, and oxy-acetylene gas cutting equipment, alongside green sand molding, core making, and non-ferrous melting furnace setups.
equipment: AC/DC Shielded Metal Arc Welding (SMAW) Sets
MIG/MAG & TIG Inert Gas Welding Stations
Oxy-Acetylene Gas Welding and Flame Cutting Kit
Foundry Pit Furnace for Non-Ferrous Casting
Green Sand Preparation Muller and Permeability Meter
Welding Inspection Gauges and Non-Destructive Testing Dye Sets
objectives: Developing sound fabrication skills across multiple fusion welding modalities
Understanding heat-affected zones (HAZ) and weld microstructure integrity
Conducting pattern making, sand conditioning, and metal pouring experiments
Analyzing casting defects like blowholes, shrinkage cavities, and porosity

engineering-drawing-lab.name: Engineering Drawing Lab
engineering-drawing-lab.description: The Engineering Drawing Lab serves as the foundational laboratory where engineering visualization, orthographic projection, sectional views, and assembly drawing fundamentals are developed. Equipped with professional drafting boards, draftettes, and high-precision drawing instruments, students learn standard engineering drawing conventions, dimensioning, tolerances, and geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T).
equipment: Professional Drafting Tables with Adjustable Tilt Angles
Engineering Scale Rules and Drawing Instrument Kits
3D Geometric Projection Solids and Model Displays
Interactive Projection and Drafting Demonstration System
objectives: Mastering first-angle and third-angle orthographic projection standards
Developing sectional, isometric, and perspective views of complex components
Applying GD&T symbols and standard ISO limits and fits
Translating manual drafts into computer-aided engineering models

cad-cam-lab.name: CAD and Simulation Lab
cad-cam-lab.description: The CAD and Simulation Lab provides students with high-performance computing workstations equipped with modern design and manufacturing software packages. Students learn parametric 3D solid modeling, computer-aided manufacturing toolpath generation, G-code/M-code programming for CNC equipment, and discrete-event system simulation for industrial assembly lines and supply chains.
equipment: Arena & FlexSim Discrete Event Simulation Software
CNC G-Code Simulator and CAM Toolpath Verifier
High-Speed Plotter and Multi-format Industrial Printers
objectives: Modeling parametric complex mechanical parts and multi-part assemblies
Simulating production line bottlenecks and queueing behaviors in manufacturing
Generating and verifying CNC machine toolpaths for automated fabrication
Optimizing plant layouts and material flow using digital twin methodologies

machine-tool-lab.name: Materials Handling & Maintenance Engineering Lab
machine-tool-lab.description: The Materials Handling & Maintenance Engineering Lab emphasizes the analysis, design, and preventative maintenance of modern material handling equipment, automated conveyors, and production machinery. Students study vibration analysis, condition monitoring, hydraulic and pneumatic actuators, lubricant tribology, and overall equipment effectiveness (OEE).
equipment: Belt and Roller Conveyor Experimental Modules
Acoustic Emission and Stroboscopic Tachometer Units
Industrial Lubricant Viscometer and Flash Point Testers
objectives: Designing unit load and bulk material handling systems for factory floors
Implementing Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) and predictive condition monitoring
Analyzing fluid power circuits (hydraulic and pneumatic) for automation
Measuring vibration signatures to detect bearing failures and shaft misalignments

ergonomics-safety-management-lab.name: Ergonomics & Safety Management Lab
ergonomics-safety-management-lab.description: The Ergonomics & Safety Management Lab focuses on human factors engineering, occupational biomechanics, workplace environment assessment, and industrial safety compliance. Students use anthropometric measurement tools, environmental meters (lux, sound, heat stress), and biomechanical posture analysis methods to design human-centered workplaces that minimize musculoskeletal disorders and optimize productivity.
equipment: Anthropometric Measurement Kits and Sliding Calipers
Sound Level Meters (A/C Weighting with Octave Band Analyzer)
Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) Heat Stress Monitor
Goniometers, Hand Grip Dynamometers & Pinch Gauges
Digital Push-Pull Force Gauges and Ergonomic Evaluation Software
objectives: Conducting anthropometric surveys to design ergonomic workstations and chairs
Evaluating indoor environmental quality including illumination, noise, and thermal comfort
Applying posture assessment tools (RULA, REBA, OWAS) for worker safety
Formulating comprehensive OSHA-aligned hazard mitigation and safety protocols

measurement-quality-control-lab.name: Measurement, Instrumentation and Quality Control Lab
measurement-quality-control-lab.description: The Measurement, Instrumentation and Quality Control Lab is equipped with high-precision linear, angular, and surface texture measuring instruments, alongside digital calibration and statistical quality control (SQC) systems. Students verify tolerances, calibrate gauges, build control charts (X-bar, R, p-charts), and conduct acceptance sampling and gauge repeatability and reproducibility (Gage R&R) studies.
equipment: Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM) Trainer & Optical Comparators
Digital Vernier Calipers, Micrometers, and Height Gauges (0.001mm)
Surface Roughness Testers with Profile Tracing
Sine Bars, Slip Gauge Sets (Grade 0 and Grade 1), and Angle Dekkors
Digital Bevel Protractors and Dial Bore Gauges
Statistical Process Control (SPC) Quality Analysis Software
objectives: Calibrating precision dimensional inspection equipment to traceable standards
Measuring micro-inch surface roughness and waviness profiles
Executing Gage R&R studies to assess measurement system variance
Constructing statistical control charts to detect process variation and defects

metrology-lab.name: Metallurgy Lab
metrology-lab.description: The Metallurgy Lab is dedicated to the characterization of metallic materials, alloy microstructures, phase transformations, and thermal treatment processes. Equipped with metallurgical microscopes, polishing tables, specimen mounting presses, and electric muffle furnaces, students analyze iron-carbon equilibrium phases, grain size, case hardening, and precipitation kinetics.
equipment: Trinocular Metallurgical Microscopes with Digital Image Analysis
Rotary Disc Grinding and Polishing Machines
Chemical Etching Reagents and Fume Extraction Hood
objectives: Preparing metallographic specimens via sectioning, mounting, grinding, and polishing
Observing ferrite, pearlite, martensite, and austenite microstructures in steels
Evaluating the impact of annealing, normalizing, quenching, and tempering on hardness
Quantifying ASTM grain size numbers and grain boundary distribution

strength-of-materials-lab.name: Strength of Materials Lab
strength-of-materials-lab.description: The Strength of Materials Lab provides essential testing facilities to verify theoretical mechanics and evaluate mechanical properties of metallic and composite specimens. Equipped with universal testing machines, torsion testers, impact testers, and hardness apparatus, students test tension, compression, shear, bending, and torsion under calibrated loading.
equipment: Computerized Universal Testing Machine (UTM) with Extensometer
Torsion Testing Machine with Angle of Twist Encoders
Charpy and Izod Pendulum Impact Tester
Rockwell, Brinell, and Vickers Hardness Testers
Beam Bending and Deflection Experimental Test Rigs
Electrical Resistance Strain Gauge Indicator Stations
objectives: Determining yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and modulus of elasticity
Measuring toughness and notch sensitivity under dynamic impact loading
Investigating pure torsion shear stresses and angle of twist in shafts
Validating Euler buckling formulas for columns under varying end constraints

mechanics-of-machinery-lab.name: Mechanics of Machinery Lab
mechanics-of-machinery-lab.description: The Mechanics of Machinery Lab provides practical experimentation in kinematic mechanisms, gear trains, dynamic balancing of rotating masses, vibration damping, and gyroscopic principles. Students observe velocity and acceleration profiles in linkages and study resonant frequencies under forced vibrations.
equipment: Dynamic and Static Balancing Demonstration Rigs
Whirling of Shafts Experimental Setup with Variable Speed Motor
Cam and Follower Displacement and Jump Analysis Kit
Epicyclic and Compound Gear Train Efficiency Apparatus
objectives: Balancing single-plane and multi-plane rotating unbalance masses dynamically
Analyzing gyroscopic precessional torque on spinning rotors
Measuring critical whirling speeds of shafts with diverse boundary conditions
Determining speed regulation sensitivity and stability of mechanical governors

fluid-mechanics-and-machinery-lab.name: Fluid Mechanics and Machinery Lab
fluid-mechanics-and-machinery-lab.description: The Fluid Mechanics and Machinery Lab features comprehensive fluid circuits, flow measurement benches, and hydraulic turbomachinery demonstrators. Students explore laminar and turbulent flow dynamics, pipe friction losses, Reynolds numbers, Bernoulli principles, and the performance characteristics of centrifugal pumps, Pelton wheels, and Francis turbines.
equipment: Hydraulic Bench with Variable Flow Recirculation Sump
Venturi Meter, Orifice Plate, and Rotameter Flow Meter Benches
Pipe Friction Loss and Minor Loss Pipework Apparatus
Centrifugal Pump Test Rig with Pressure Transducers
objectives: Verifying Bernoulli Theorem and computing discharge coefficients for flowmeters
Measuring Darcy-Weisbach friction factors and minor head losses across pipe fittings
Generating pump characteristic curves (head, flow rate, brake power, efficiency)
Evaluating hydraulic turbine power output and runaway speed under variable loads

thermodynamics-heat-transfer-lab.name: Thermodynamics & Heat Transfer Lab
thermodynamics-heat-transfer-lab.description: The Thermodynamics & Heat Transfer Lab facilitates in-depth investigations of thermal energy conversion, refrigeration cycles, and heat transfer phenomena. Students evaluate linear and radial thermal conduction, free and forced convection, Stefan-Boltzmann radiation, shell-and-tube heat exchangers, and vapor compression refrigeration cycles.
equipment: Free and Forced Convection Pin-Fin Heat Transfer Unit
Concentric Tube & Shell-and-Tube Heat Exchanger Test Benches
Stefan-Boltzmann Radiation and Emissivity Measurement Unit
Vapor Compression Refrigeration Cycle Test Simulator
Digital Temperature Data Acquisition and Thermocouple Arrays
objectives: Calculating thermal conductivity (k) and overall heat transfer coefficients (U)
Comparing parallel flow and counter flow configurations in heat exchangers
Measuring emissivity of surfaces and validating radiation physics
Evaluating the Coefficient of Performance (COP) in refrigeration systems
